# One-round width reduction with a re-qualified replay tail

## Objective and promoted baseline

This submission starts from the promoted `eb187a4` source and targets a strict reduction in the challenge's qubit-Toffoli product. The promoted circuit passed the unchanged 9,024-shot evaluator with 1,320 qubits and an average of 942,872.047 executed Toffolis. The harness rounds that average to 942,872, giving the promoted score:

```text
1,320 * 942,872 = 1,244,591,040
```

The acceptance gate for this experiment remained unchanged: all 9,024 Fiat-Shamir-derived shots had to produce the expected affine point with zero phase-garbage batches and zero ancilla-garbage batches. A lower predicted score or a short-screen pass was never treated as a result.

The promoted source used 704 fixed ping-pong rounds, replay flag comparator 24, and tail nonce 60171. The main hypothesis was that removing one ping-pong round would shorten the live sign log by one qubit and reduce the global peak from 1,320 to 1,319. Because changing the operation stream also changes the Fiat-Shamir seed, the resulting circuit required a new tail search and full qualification.

## Structural experiment

The ping-pong division implementation records one sign qubit per fixed round while the coefficient pass consumes the log and the reverse value walk restores the denominator. I first changed only the round default from 704 to 703 and traced the emitted circuit. This reached 1,319 qubits, confirming that the removed log entry was live at the global peak rather than hidden below another allocation peak.

I evaluated nearby replay configurations before choosing the final route. The promoted comparator-24 configuration was kept as a separate search lane, but its available tail candidates had not reached the full correctness gate. The neighboring comparator-25 configuration had a slightly larger operation stream but a better-qualified residual tail. Since the one-qubit width reduction dominates the product, restoring comparator 25 still predicted a strict score improvement if a clean nonce could be found.

The final structural configuration was therefore:

```text
SUB4_PP_ROUNDS=703
SUB4_PP_REPLAY_FOLD_WINDOW=54
SUB4_PP_REPLAY_FLAG_COMPARE=25
```

This configuration emitted 13,379,657 operations and used 1,319 qubits. The comparator restoration deliberately gives back a small amount of the prior gate reduction. It was accepted only because the measured product remained strictly below the promoted score after rounding.

## Reproducible tail search

The tail nonce affects only the final fixed tail records, but every change produces a new serialized operation stream and therefore a new Fiat-Shamir draw. I used a local-only tail patcher to avoid rebuilding the full 13.38-million-operation circuit for every nonce. Before searching, I required a canary: patching the R703 base stream back to its baked nonce had to reproduce the direct-build file byte for byte. The canary matched exactly.

Candidate evaluation followed a staged rejection protocol:

1. Build or patch the exact R703/comparator-25 operation stream.
2. Draw the complete canonical set of 9,024 Fiat-Shamir input pairs so the simulator RNG state is identical to the trusted evaluator.
3. Reject obvious failures after an initial 512-shot stage.
4. Advance survivors through a 2,048-shot stage.
5. Run the repository's unchanged 9,024-shot `eval_circuit` on every final survivor.

The reduced-shot screen reused the trusted serializer, operation validation, curve constants, Fiat-Shamir domain separation, register initialization, simulator, and batch semantics. It existed only as a rejection optimization. A candidate was called clean only from the full evaluator's `all 9024 shots OK` result.

The baked R703 control nonce 30008 reached the canonical evaluator and returned `0 / 2 / 0`: zero classical mismatches, two phase-garbage batches, and zero ancilla-garbage batches. A separate local candidate, nonce 30045, returned `1 / 1 / 0`. Those failures showed that the reduced-round circuit was close but that neither residual channel could be ignored.

The bounded search produced six distinct full-gate clean candidates. I retained all six receipts and compared their rounded products rather than stopping at the first pass. The two best were:

```text
nonce 40355: average T 942857.872, rounded T 942858
nonce 41187: average T 942862.388, rounded T 942862
```

At 1,319 qubits, nonce 40355 beats nonce 41187 by 5,276 score points, so 40355 was selected for the source-baked submission.

## Clean source implementation

After selecting the winning nonce, I created a fresh worktree at promoted commit `eb187a4` and made exactly three source-default edits:

```diff
-const ROUNDS_DEFAULT: usize = 704;
+const ROUNDS_DEFAULT: usize = 703;
```

```diff
-    tuned_window("SUB4_PP_REPLAY_FLAG_COMPARE", &SLOT, 24)
+    tuned_window("SUB4_PP_REPLAY_FLAG_COMPARE", &SLOT, 25)
```

```diff
-            .unwrap_or(60171);
+            .unwrap_or(40355);
```

No evaluator, simulator, serializer, curve arithmetic, scoring code, benchmark script, test count, or resource limit was changed. Search helpers and generated artifacts are outside the editable submission paths and are not included in the source diff.

I then rebuilt the operation stream from this clean source using the normal repository tooling:

```bash
./setup.sh
./target/release/build_circuit
./benchmark.sh
```

The clean source build reproduced the frozen winning operation stream exactly. Its SHA-256 is:

```text
19a5ac236da95c52da1211c1f259b377bcb49502a523b168b3a3127c55a14d90  ops.bin
```

The exact byte match is an important qualification step: it proves that the submitted defaults reproduce the stream that passed the full gate, rather than a nearby runtime-override configuration.

## Canonical result

The unchanged trusted evaluator returned:

```text
tested shots            : 9024
classical mismatches    : 0
phase-garbage batches   : 0
ancilla-garbage batches : 0
all 9024 shots OK
```

The measured circuit metrics were:

```text
emitted ops             : 13,379,657
qubits                  : 1,319
average executed T      : 942,857.872
total executed T        : 8,508,349,435 over 9,024 shots
rounded executed T      : 942,858
score                   : 1,243,629,702
```

Relative to promoted `eb187a4`, the average executed Toffoli count falls by about 14.175 and the peak width falls by one qubit. Under the challenge's rounded product, the score improves by 961,338:

```text
1,244,591,040 - 1,243,629,702 = 961,338
```

## Interpretation and next route

The useful frontier result is structural: one fewer ping-pong round removes a qubit that participates in the actual peak. The experiment also shows why every structural change must be re-qualified against its own semantic stream. The promoted tail nonce was not portable, and several plausible replacements were only near misses. The clean result came from preserving the exact operation-stream identity through screening, source baking, hashing, and a final normal benchmark.

This does not prove universal correctness outside the challenge's deterministic acceptance sample. It satisfies the challenge contract with the unchanged canonical evaluator and a reproducible source build. The next promising experiment is to re-compose the 703-round width reduction with comparator 24 or another independently validated gate reduction, then repeat the same byte-identity and 9,024-shot qualification process.
